slides.title: 3 scams hitting young adults
slides.sub: 40% of money-loss scam reports from ages 18 to 29 started on social media in 2025.

slides.heading: #1 Fake shop ads
body: You order from an ad on Instagram or TikTok, and the item never shows up or it's a cheap knockoff. More than 40% of people who lost money to a social media scam said it started with an ad.
Before you buy, search the store's name plus "scam" or "reviews". Pay with a credit card if you can, so you can dispute the charge.

slides.heading: #2 Fake rentals
body: Scammers copy real listings, change the contact info, and ask for a deposit or "holding fee" before you've seen the place. The median reported loss was $1,000.
People 18 to 29 were 3 times as likely as other adults to lose money to one. Never pay until you've toured in person.
slides.source: FTC Data Spotlight, Dec. 2025 (reports Jan. 2020 to June 2025)

slides.heading: #3 Fake jobs
body: A "recruiter" texts you about an easy, high-paying job, then asks for your Social Security number or bank info, or sends a link that installs spyware.
Job seekers lost almost $300 million to job scams in the first half of 2025. Real employers never make you pay to get hired.
slides.source: FTC data, Jan. to June 2025, via Fortune

slides.heading: Where scams start
slides.intro: Share of money-loss scam reports that started on social media, 2025

slides.takeaway: One rule covers all three: never pay first for something you can't verify.

posts.caption:
Scammers go where young people scroll. In 2025, 40% of money-loss scam reports from 18 to 29-year-olds started on social media, the highest of any age group (FTC). Reported losses to social media scams hit $2.1 billion, about eight times 2020's level.

The 3 to know: fake shop ads (the most reported scam that starts on social media), fake rentals (18 to 29-year-olds were 3 times as likely as other adults to report losing money, median loss $1,000) and fake jobs (almost $300 million lost to job scams in the first half of 2025).

The rule that covers all three: never pay first for something you can't verify. Tour a rental before you pay, and real employers never make you pay to get hired.

Data: FTC Data Spotlights (April 2026 and December 2025) and FTC job scam data via Fortune (November 2025).
